stem: The function $f(x) = {=a}\cos(x - {=p}^\circ) + {=q}$ can also be written in the form $f(x) = {=a}\sin(x + h^\circ) + {=q}$, where $-180 < h \le 180$. Find the value of $h$.
solution: Use the shift rule for the two graphs: $\cos\theta = \sin(\theta + 90^\circ)$, so the cosine graph is the sine graph shifted $90^\circ$ to the left.
Here the angle is $\theta = x - {=p}^\circ$, so $\cos(x - {=p}^\circ) = \sin(x - {=p}^\circ + 90^\circ)$. The amplitude ${=a}$ and the vertical shift ${=q}$ do not change.
Combine the two angles: $-{=p}^\circ + 90^\circ = {=h}^\circ$, so $f(x) = {=a}\sin(x + h^\circ) + {=q}$ with $h = {=h}$.
notes: No figure. The book's questions read two sine/cosine graphs from a diagram; this advanced family works on the stated objective sentence instead (cos θ = sin(θ + 90°)) and adds the twist that the angle is x - p rather than plain θ, so the learner must substitute into the book's identity and combine the shifts. Answer is h = 90 - p, checked numerically for all 12 values of p (p = 90 excluded because h would be 0); h ranges over -70..70, always inside the stated window -180 < h <= 180, so it is unique and no mod-360 ambiguity arises. Negative h (p > 90) is deliberate: it tests the sign of the shift. Only the book's own identity and its meaning as a horizontal shift are used; no reduction formulas or negative-angle identities.
